entries.title: Psalms 30:1
segments: Title:  others render this title thus:  A Psalm, a Song of dedication for the house, by David; and they suppose the reference to be to the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, which David purchased upon the occasion of the pestilence with which Israel was visited for his sin in numbering the people.  Of this David said, "This is the house of the Lord God,"
, and it seems probable, from the verses that follow, that he then dedicated that spot as the site of the future temple.  With this supposition the contents of the psalm well agree.

entries.title: Psalms 30:2
segments: Prayer is the grand means of deliverance from trouble; and when deliverance is granted, devout praises should be rendered to God, the author and giver of all good.

entries.title: Psalms 30:6
segments: Continued prosperity often leads men to forget their dependence on God, and makes affliction needful to teach them that all their blessings come from him.

entries.title: Psalms 30:7
segments: Made my mountain to stand strong; given me steadfast prosperity.

entries.title: Psalms 30:11
segments: God brings his people out of trouble, that they may unite in praising and adoring him.

entries.title: Psalms 30:12
segments: My glory; my soul, as the word is elsewhere used.  See note to
, where the word in the original is the same as here.
